nodes.statement: Suppose that X is an object in KInj^b(k G). Thinking of H^*(G,X) as Hom_KInj(k G)(ik,X), it follows from the hypothesis that if Y is in Thick(ik) then Hom_KInj(k G)(Y,X) is finitely generated as a module over H^*(G,k). In the case of a finite p-group, the module k G, regarded as an element of D^b(k G) concentrated in a single degree, is in Thick(ik), as it is built from |G| copies of k. So Hom_KInj(k G)(k G,X) is finitely generated. But it is also killed by the ideal of positive (cohomological) degree elements, so it is finite dimensional. But Hom_KInj(k G)(k G,X) is the cohomology of X as a complex. So X is exact in all but finitely many degrees, and is hence equivalent to a semi-injective resolution of an object in D^b(k G).

nodes.statement: Let X be an object in KInj^b(k G). Since H^*(G,X) is finitely generated over H^*(G,k), there exists nin mathbb Z such that H^i(G,X)=0 for i< n. Assuming without loss of generality that X is minimal, we have Hom_k G(k,X^i)=0 for i< n. Then the (brutal) truncation X^< n is in KInj^0(k G), and the inclusion X^geqslant nto X is a cohomology equivalence. We may now assume that X^i=0 for i<n. Then there is a finite dimensional summand Y^n of X^n such that the inclusion induces an isomorphism Hom_k G(k,Y^n) to Hom_k G(k,X^n). Next, there is a finite dimensional summand Y^n+1 of X^n+1 which contains the image of Y^n under the differential, and such that Hom_k G(k,Y^n+1) to Hom_k G(k,X^n+1) is an isomorphism. Continuing this way, we construct a subcomplex Y of X which is a summand in each degree, so that it is a complex of injectives, and such that the quotient X/Y is in KInj^0(k G). Then the inclusion Y to X is a cohomology equivalence.

$H^i(G,X)=0$ for $i< n$. 
Assuming without loss of generality that $X$ is minimal, we have
$\mathsf{Hom}_{k G}(k,X^i)=0$ for $i< n$. Then the (brutal)
truncation $X^{< n}$ is in $\mathsf{KInj}^0(k G)$, and the inclusion 
$X^{\geqslant  n}\to X$ is a cohomology equivalence. 

We may now assume that $X^i=0$ for $i<n$. Then there is a finite
dimensional summand $Y^n$ of $X^n$ such that the inclusion
induces an isomorphism $\mathsf{Hom}_{k G}(k,Y^n) \to \mathsf{Hom}_{k G}(k,X^n)$.

isomorphism. Continuing this way, we construct a subcomplex $Y$ of $X$
which is a summand in each degree, so that it is a complex of
injectives, and such that the quotient $X/Y$ is in
$\mathsf{KInj}^0(k G)$. Then the inclusion $Y \to X$ is a cohomology equivalence.

We begin by showing that Conjecture~\ref{conj:strong-stmod} implies
Conjecture~\ref{conj:strong-Db} and Conjecture~\ref{conj:weak-stmod}
implies Conjecture~\ref{conj:weak-Db}. 
  
Let $X$ be an object in $\mathsf{KInj}^{\mathsf{b}}(k G)$.
Replacing $X$ by the
cohomologically equivalent $v_\rho v X$, which we may do in both
Conjecture~\ref{conj:strong-Db} and Conjecture~\ref{conj:weak-Db},
we may suppose that $X$ is in $\mathsf{Loc}(\mathsf{ik})$. Using
Proposition~\ref{pr:whittle-down} and
shifting if necessary we may assume that $X^n=0$ for $n<0$.  
By Corollary~\ref{co:tX}, $\mathsf{tk} \otimes X$ is a Tate resolution of a
$k G$-module $M$ in $\mathsf{StMod}^b(k G)\cap \mathsf{Loc}(\mathsf{ik})$. 

If
Conjecture~\ref{conj:strong-stmod} holds, there is a finitely generated
$k G$-module $M'\in \mathsf{stmod}(k G)$ such that $M\to M'$ is a cohomology
equivalence; whereas if Conjecture~\ref{conj:weak-stmod} holds then
$M$ is a module in $\mathsf{Thick}(\mathsf{stmod}(k G),\mathsf{StMod}^0(k G))$, and we set
$M'=M$.

The module $M'$ is
only well defined up to adding and removing projective summands, but we
regard it as an object in $\mathsf{Mod}(k G)$.
Then the complex $\mathsf{ik} \otimes M'$ is an injective resolution of $M'$, and 
may be regarded as an object in 
$\mathsf{D}^{\mathsf{b}}(k G)\subseteq\mathsf{KInj}(k G)$, respectively $\mathsf{Thick}(\mathsf{D}^{\mathsf{b}}(k G),\mathsf{KInj}^0(k G))$,
giving us a diagram
\[ \xymatrix@=6mm{\mathsf{pk} \otimes X \ar[r] & X \ar[r]\ar@{.>}[d]
 & \mathsf{tk}\otimes X = \mathsf{t}M\ar[d] \\
&\mathsf{ik} \otimes M' \ar[r]& \mathsf{tk} \otimes M' \ar[r] & \Sigma \mathsf{pk} \otimes M'.} \]
Since $X^n=0$ for $n<0$, and $(\Sigma\mathsf{pk}\otimes M')^n=0$ for $n\geqslant 0$, 
 there are no no-zero maps from $X$ to $\Sigma
\mathsf{pk} \otimes M'$. So we can fill
in the dotted arrow to make the diagram above commutative. This dotted
arrow is an isomorphism in cohomology in sufficiently large degrees.
Complete this to a triangle
\[ Y \to X \to \mathsf{ik}\otimes M' \to \Sigma Y. \]
Then $Y$ has cohomology only in finitely many degrees, and is in
$\mathsf{Loc}(\mathsf{ik})$, so it is in $\mathsf{D}^{\mathsf{b}}(k G)$. Since $\mathsf{ik} \otimes M'$ is  in
$\mathsf{D}^{\mathsf{b}}(k G)$, respectively $\mathsf{Thick}(\mathsf{D}^{\mathsf{b}}(k G),\mathsf{KInj}^0(k G))$ 
it follows that $X$ is. This completes the proof that
Conjecture~\ref{conj:strong-stmod} implies
Conjecture~\ref{conj:strong-Db} and that
Conjecture~\ref{conj:weak-stmod} imples Conjecture~\ref{conj:weak-Db}.

Conversely, 
let $M$ be a module in $\mathsf{StMod}^b(k G)$. We may suppose that $M$ has no
projective summands. Then $\mathsf{ik} \otimes M$ is an
object in $\mathsf{KInj}^{\mathsf{b}}(k G)$. If Conjecture~\ref{conj:strong-Db} holds,
then 
there is an object $X$ in $\mathsf{D}^{\mathsf{b}}(k G)$
that is cohomology equivalent to $\mathsf{ik}\otimes M$; whereas if
Conjecture~\ref{conj:weak-Db} holds, then $\mathsf{ik}\otimes M$ is in
$\mathsf{Thick}(\mathsf{D}^{\mathsf{b}}(k G),\mathsf{KInj}^0(k G))$, and we set $X=\mathsf{ik}\otimes M$.
Then $\mathsf{tk}\otimes X$
is in $\mathsf{stmod}(k G)$, respectively $\mathsf{Thick}(\mathsf{stmod}(k G),\mathsf{StMod}^0(k G))$, 
and is cohomology equivalent to $M$.

nodes.statement: Since we've shown that Conjecture~ implies the remaining conjectures, we prove Conjecture~ in this case. If Theta_Gsubseteq\0\ and M is a module in StMod^f(k G) then by Theorem~, M decomposes as a direct sum of a module in Loc(k) and a no cohomology module. So M is cohomologically equivalent to a module in Loc(k), and hence without loss of generality M is in Loc(k). So Ext^*_k G(C,M) is finitely generated over H^*(G,k) whenever C is in the thick subcategory generated by k and the no cohomology modules. In particular, if S is a Sylow p-subgroup of G then the permutation module k(G/S) decomposes as a direct sum of a module in Thick(k) and a no cohomology module. So Ext^*_k G(k(G/S),M) is finitely generated over H^*(G,k).
